intro: Google Play marks every Android app with one of five desktop tags for Googlebooks. These are the apps press reviews and Google have named with a tag; the list is not complete, and tags change. Open the Play Store on your Googlebook to see the current tag on each app.

apps.name: Adobe Photoshop
apps.note: Google's headline example. Reviewers note it is the limited Android version, not the full desktop Photoshop.

apps.name: Luminar
apps.note: Rebuilt for Googlebook. One review found no pinch or rotate gestures on the trackpad.

apps.name: Fantastical
apps.note: The calendar app skipped Android phones and launched on Googlebooks first.
apps.source: Android Police, Oct 2026; Tom's Hardware, Oct 2026

apps.name: Notability
apps.note: Google's own example of an adaptive app: its canvas and toolbars reflow as you resize the window, and keyboard and trackpad support carry over.
apps.source: Google Googlebook announcement; Tom's Hardware, Oct 2026

apps.name: CapCut
apps.note: Named by Google as one of the roughly 20 apps in the top two tiers at launch.

apps.name: Netflix
apps.note: Listed among the major apps optimized or made for desktop.

apps.name: Obsidian
apps.note: Listed among the major apps optimized or made for desktop.

apps.name: Zoom
apps.note: Listed among the major apps optimized or made for desktop.

apps.name: Microsoft 365 (Office)
apps.note: Microsoft Office is listed among the major apps optimized or made for desktop.

apps.name: Spotify
apps.note: Carries the Optimized tag, though one reviewer found it scales poorly on a 14-inch screen.

apps.name: Apple Music
apps.note: Tagged Optimized for desktop and chosen automatically when you set a Googlebook up from your phone.

apps.name: Facebook
apps.note: The Play Store points you to the website instead of the app, and it is not moved over automatically during setup.

apps.name: Twitch
apps.note: The Play Store steers you to the website rather than the Android app.
